title: MIRA: Medical Time Series Foundation Model for Real-World Health Data
methods: Continuous-time positional encoding, frequency MoE and Neural ODE forecasting.
findings: Claims 454B public medical time points and cross-domain forecasting gains.
limitations: Current downloaded v7 states a Dec 2025 update; model-size and downstream fine-tuning memory must be checked before selection.
notes: Primary source; code repository returned HTTP 200 during this audit.

title: TSPFN: A Temporal Tabular Foundation Model for Physiological Time Series Classification

locators.C003: pp. 1–7; 7.3M parameter comparison and single-H200 pretraining

methods: TabPFN-like in-context learner with temporal/channel embeddings; 140k physiological sequences.
limitations: Its H200 pretraining is not evidence that pretraining is feasible on dual L40.
notes: Repository link given in paper; verified reachable.

title: medR: Reward Engineering for Clinical Offline Reinforcement Learning via Tri-Drive Potential Functions
methods: LLM-guided potential-based reward design with survival, confidence and intervention-cost components.
findings: Defines stale-measurement decay and action-magnitude penalties in addition to physiological potential.
limitations: Treatment-policy OPE does not validate numerical forecasting or causal benefit.
notes: Best recent full-text reward-design candidate found.

title: Fine-Tuning Foundation Models with Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Medical Time Series Forecasting
methods: Fine-tunes small Chronos across federated ECG/ICG clients.
findings: Local tuning can beat FL under non-IID partitions; results depend on client distribution.
limitations: Does not report dual-L40 post-training measurements or influenza data.
notes: Direct evidence for small-model medical forecasting fine-tuning.

title: Exploring a Graph-based Approach to Offline Reinforcement Learning for Sepsis Treatment
methods: GNN state encoder plus dBCQ on MIMIC-III sepsis trajectories.
findings: Reports three NVIDIA L40 GPUs with 46GB each; policy GPU training about 2.5 hours, GNN autoencoders about 30 hours.
limitations: WIS and a single MIMIC-III cohort cannot establish clinical benefit.
notes: Concrete near-match to the requested hardware, but a treatment-decision paper.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
methods: Scale, quantize and autoregressively sample time-series tokens.
findings: Open probabilistic forecasting baseline with code/weights.
limitations: Original corpus is not a medical foundation corpus; discretization has range and resolution limits.
notes: Small model family, directly usable baseline.

title: Lag-Llama: Towards Foundation Models for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting

locators.C001: pp. 3–7; univariate Student-t model and P100 training

methods: Lag covariates with decoder-only Transformer and Student-t likelihood.
findings: Probability forecasts and low-resource experimental setup.
limitations: Univariate design and pretraining corpus are not specific to elderly influenza.
notes: Open baseline; per-task memory test required.

title: MOMENT: A Family of Open Time-series Foundation Models
methods: Masked-patch encoder for multi-task time-series representations.
findings: 40M version exists; short-horizon zero-shot statistical methods can remain stronger.
limitations: Not medical-specific and not an autoregressive probabilistic forecaster.
notes: Useful representation baseline, not default flu predictor.

title: Flusion: Integrating multiple data sources for accurate influenza predictions

locators.C006: pp. 3–17; data, model and ablation tables

methods: Joint multi-signal/multi-location quantile boosting plus Bayesian ARX.
findings: Joint signal/location GBQR drives performance more than ensembling.
limitations: US surveillance target is not elderly-specific and data revisions matter.
notes: Most direct influenza forecasting research baseline.

title: PTB-XL, a large publicly available electrocardiography dataset
methods: 12-lead ECG corpus with reports and labels.
limitations: ECG classification is not influenza forecasting.

title: MIMIC-IV Clinical Database

locators.C007: PhysioNet access policy and dataset page

methods: Deidentified hospital and ICU EHR database.
findings: Longitudinal clinical events/labs/vitals can support temporal prediction tasks.
limitations: Credentialing, DUA and deidentification shift dates; not a direct public-download dataset.
notes: Core clinical benchmark with restricted-access workflow.

title: HiRID: a high time-resolution ICU dataset
findings: Explicitly supports dense irregular clinical time-series work.
limitations: Credentialed access; population/site differs from US influenza surveillance.
notes: Good stress test for irregular sampling.

title: CDC FluSight Forecast Hub
methods: Versioned probabilistic influenza forecast submissions and target data.
findings: Public reproducible forecasting target and scoring workflow.
limitations: Data revisions and all-age target require explicit vintage handling and age-specific extension.
notes: Primary target source for this project.

title: Large language models in medical time series analysis

locators.C003: pp. 1–4, review scope and resource repository

methods: Review of medical time-series LLM architectures, resources and evaluations.
findings: Maps the heterogeneous MedTSLLM literature and maintains a resource list.
limitations: A review; individual results require original-paper verification.
notes: Recent map source, not performance evidence.
